title: ipc-toolkit: the collision part of a simulator

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When two objects touch in a physics simulation, somebody has to figure out exactly where and how. ipc-toolkit is the library that answers that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, and that's the design. It provides geometric building blocks for contact-aware simulation. Your own simulation keeps control of time stepping and the solve loop, and calls the library for collision questions.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It handles collision meshes, a broad-phase step that quickly finds which pieces might touch, and continuous collision detection, which catches a hit that happens between two frames. It also provides contact-related energies and friction.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The project describes itself as a friction and contact toolkit for robust computer graphics and finite element simulation. Clean boundaries make it easy to drop into someone else's solver.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This is a fork, with the upstream project credited. It's mostly C plus plus, built with CMake, with a Python layer and tests in Catch2.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. The full page lays out the library boundary in more detail.
